{{short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Newman molchanov gaertner.jpg|thumb|From left: Charles Newman, Stanislav Molchanov, Jürgen Gärtner, Oberwolfach 2003]]
'''Jürgen Gärtner''' (born 1950) is a German mathematician, specializing in [[probability theory]] and [[analysis]].

== Biography ==
Gärtner was born in 1950 in [[Reichenbach (Oberlausitz)|Reichenbach]]. He graduated in 1973 with ''[[Diplom]]'' from [[TU Dresden]]. He received in 1976 his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[Lomonosov University]] under the supervision of [[Mark Freidlin]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=30768}}</ref> At the [[Weierstrass Institute]], Gärtner was from 1976 to 1985 a research associate; he habilitated there in 1984 with Dissertation B: ''Zur Ausbreitung von Wellenfronten für Reaktions-Diffusions-Gleichungen'' (The propagation of wave fronts for reaction-diffusion equations). At the Weierstrass Institute he was from 1985 to 1995 the head of the probability group. He was a professor of the Academy of Sciences of the GDR from 1988 until its disbandment in late 1991. At TU Berlin he was from 1992 to 2011 a professor, retiring as professor emeritus in 2011.<ref name="CV">{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae of Prof. Jürgen Gärtner|website=tu-berlin.de|url=http://page.math.tu-berlin.de/~jg/jg_files/cv.pdf}}</ref>

In 1977 he proved a general form of [[Cramér's theorem (large deviations)|Cramér's Theorem]] in the theory of [[large deviations]] (LD);<ref>{{cite journal|author=Gärtner, J.|title=On large deviations from the invariant measure|journal=Theory of Probability and Its Applications|volume=22|year=1977|pages=24–39|doi=10.1137/1122003}}</ref> the theorem is known as the Gärtner-Ellis Large Deviations Principle (LDP). ([[Richard S. Ellis]] proved the theorem in 1984 with weaker premises.) In 1982 Gärtner wrote an important paper on the famous [[KPP equation]] (a semi-linear diffusion equation introduced in 1937).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Gärtner, J.|title=Location of wave fronts for the multidimensional KPP equation and Brownian first exit densities|journal=Math. Nachr.|volume=105|year=1982|pages=317–351|doi=10.1002/mana.19821050117}}</ref> In 1987 Gärtner, with [[Donald A. Dawson]], introduced the construction of a [[projective limit]] in the LDP. From 1987 to 1989 Gärtner and Dawson wrote a series of important papers on the [[McKean–Vlasov process|McKean-Vlasov process]]. Their results were extended by other mathematicians in the 1990s to random mean-field interactions and to spin-glass mean-field interactions. In 1990 Gärtner and [[Stanislav Molchanov|Molchanov]] wrote a seminal paper on [[intermittency]] in the parabolic Anderson model; the paper introduced a new approach to intermittency via the study of [[Lyapunov exponent|Lyapunov coefficients]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=den Hollander, Frank|title=The mathematical work of Jürgen Gärtner|website=Workshop on Random Media in celebration of Jürgen Gärtner's 60th birthday|url=https://www3.math.tu-berlin.de/stoch/jgeb2010/JG60.pdf}}</ref>

Gärtner was a member from 1984 to 1992 of the editorial board of ''[[Probability Theory and Related Fields]]'' and from 1990 to 2000 of the editorial board of ''[[Mathematische Nachrichten]]''.<ref name=CV/>

In 1992 Gärtner was an invited lecturer at the first [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in Paris. In 1994 he was an invited speaker with talk ''Parabolic Systems in Random Media and Aspects of Intermittency'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zürich]]. A conference was held in honor of his 60th birthday.<ref>{{cite web|title=Program; Invited Speakers|url=http://www3.math.tu-berlin.de/jgeb2010/jg.html|website=Workshop on Random Media in celebration of Jürgen Gärtner's 60th birthday}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zTS7VwM5roUC|title = Probability in Complex Physical Systems: In Honour of Erwin Bolthausen and Jürgen Gärtner|isbn = 9783642238116|last1 = Deuschel|first1 = Jean-Dominique|last2 = Gentz|first2 = Barbara|last3 = König|first3 = Wolfgang|last4 = Renesse|first4 = Max von|last5 = Scheutzow|first5 = Michael|last6 = Schmock|first6 = Uwe|date = 2012-04-23| publisher=Springer}}</ref>
